placements.role: Provides large-scale electrical transmission, distribution and substation construction services.

role_evidence.claim: MYR Group's 2025 Form 10-K says its Transmission and Distribution segment designs, engineers, builds, upgrades and repairs transmission networks, distribution systems and substations.

business_summary: MYR Group Inc. is a Nasdaq-listed holding company for specialty electrical contractors in the United States and Canada. Its Transmission and Distribution segment builds and maintains transmission lines, distribution systems and substations for electric utilities; its Commercial and Industrial segment does electrical construction for buildings including data centres. It is a labour and execution business, not a manufacturer, so its margins are contract margins.

exposure_summary.narrative: MYR Group has one placement, on grid-interconnect, position three of the chain and the link the chain's own bottleneck note calls the slowest step in the entire sequence. The link is scored UNDISCOVERED with the lowest crowdedness score on the chain. The company's exposure is double-sided: the T&D segment builds the interconnection itself, and the C&I segment names data centres as one of the facility types it wires.

data_gaps: Every canonical metric in this profile resolves to a sourced number; there are no NULL canonical fields.
Companyfacts coverage for this issuer is missing inventory, which does not affect any canonical profile field but does limit working-capital analysis.
The pcs institutional-ownership field reads above 1.0, which is not a usable percentage; crowdedness on this name rests on the analyst count and axis-A instead.
No data-centre revenue share is disclosed; the C&I segment names data centres among many facility types without sizing them.
The fetched EDGAR document is the Q2 2026 8-K earnings exhibit, not the 10-K that backs the mapped role evidence.

disposition.basis: Complete medium profile on the quietest link of the chain, with the fullest measurement set after Vertiv: every canonical field sourced, Piotroski at the top of its range and Beneish clean. Retained rather than advanced because value capture at this link is contractor margin rather than equipment margin, and because the cash-conversion figure that looks strongest is the one least likely to be durable. Selection is a separate command.

confidence_audit.basis: Counts cover the canonical metric fields only. VERIFIED is a figure read directly off SEC companyfacts as reported. INFERRED is a figure computed from SEC companyfacts, with the derivation named in its basis; where a market price enters the computation the basis says so explicitly, because the price leg is the repo's own dual-source market plane (data/market/MYRG.json, price_status AGREED) and not an issuer document. SPECULATIVE is reserved for the reverse-DCF solve, whose discount rate and terminal growth are assumed. NULL is a field looked for and not found, never estimated.
